claim.quote: We find that the anti-neutrino flux agrees with that predicted in the absence of oscillations to better than 5%

date.note: arXiv submission date; published Phys. Rev. Lett. 84, 3764 (2000).

key_value_text.value: Anti-neutrino flux agrees with no-oscillation prediction to better than 5%; 90% CL exclusion for delta m^2 > 1.12e-3 eV^2 at maximal mixing

name: Search for Neutrino Oscillations at the Palo Verde Nuclear Reactors

summary.plain: First results from Palo Verde: the antineutrino flux about 800 metres from the three reactors matched the no-oscillation prediction to better than 5 per cent, excluding oscillations for mass differences above about one thousandth of an eV squared at maximal mixing.
summary.technical: Initial anti-nu_e flux and spectrum measurement at ~800 m with a segmented Gd-loaded scintillator: flux agrees with the no-oscillation prediction to better than 5 %; 90 % CL exclusion for delta m^2 > 1.12e-3 eV^2 (maximal mixing) and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.21 (large delta m^2).

title: Search for Neutrino Oscillations at the Palo Verde Nuclear Reactors
why_it_matters: The first of the Palo Verde limits, published alongside the CHOOZ results.
